title: Custom Properties
story: CSS variables (--name) hold a value once and reuse it everywhere. Change one line and the whole page changes.
goal: Define --brand on :root, then use var(--brand) for the h1 colour and the .btn background.
starter: Aata

tests.label: --brand is defined on :root
tests.js: var css0 = $$("style").map(function (s) { return s.textContent; }).join(" "); return /:root\s*{[^}]*--brand\s*:/.test(css0) || "define --brand inside :root { }"

tests.label: var(--brand) is used at least twice
tests.js: var css1 = $$("style").map(function (s) { return s.textContent; }).join(" "); return (css1.match(/var\(\s*--brand\s*\)/g) || []).length >= 2 || "use var(--brand) in two places"

tests.label: The h1 is no longer black

hints: Custom property names start with two dashes.
Aata
socratic: Why is one variable better than copying the colour?
Can a variable hold a size too?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Custom Properties”?
solution: Aata
